classifications.seam: Admits command/effect evidence only inside a fence on current product standing (a dispatch read basis, a claimed command, or a receipt-protected lifecycle transaction); calling it anywhere is the ACTION seam itself.
classifications.ledger: Writes the command ledger, command-record facts, imported command history or operational observations directly, without a current-standing fence; only a declared seam owner may call it, and every other call is a listed bypass.
classifications.product-fact: Writes product records, events, scopes, Home product-store registration and readiness, or derived projection metadata; not command/effect evidence, though the lifecycle that calls it may still owe an admitted command under ACTION-3 to ACTION-6.
classifications.home-storage: Stages both a project Home product-store binding and its separate operation-journal binding and files; this preparation writes no command/effect evidence and grants no Home activation or reference-coverage authority.
classifications.reference-journal: Writes the Home reference journal, a separate authority with its own operation, refusal and seal records; its admission is governed by its own lifecycle rather than this ledger.
classifications.configuration: Configures a handle (codec, deadline, process guard, basis combination) and persists nothing by itself.

seam_owners.reason: Owns the HTTP command envelope: it alone claims, replays and settles the command ledger row for an Idempotency-Key request before and after its handler runs.
Owns the product action outbox: durable dispatch intent, delivery to the runtime and admission of the returned receipt under stable identities.

unfenced-preparation.reason: Action input binding and policy preparation fall back to an unfenced record writer when the caller supplies no dispatch read basis, so their evidence can land without a current-standing check.
required_evidence: Require a dispatch read basis on every production caller and delete the unfenced branch.
A caller without current standing is refused before any preparation fact is written.

second-command-envelope.reason: Context-stream uploads claim and fail their own command ledger rows instead of going through the HTTP command envelope, so the ledger has a second state machine for one kind of request.
required_evidence: Route upload claims through the command envelope owner or a fenced admission with the same replay and conflict semantics.
Keep the Office task fence and legacy-key exclusion the upload claim relies on today.

gaugeapp-command-receipts.reason: GaugeApp host commands, reviews and external review completions admit their receipts and facts as chained record facts outside the dispatch fence and outside the action outbox.
required_evidence: Admit each consequential GaugeApp command through the shared product action admission with its actor, basis and receipt.
External review outcomes enter as observed results bound to the original command, never as a new author.

agent-exchange.reason: GaugeApp agent exchanges append transcript facts directly; the turn that produced them is not linked to an admitted command, attempt and outcome.
required_evidence: Bind each appended exchange to its admitted turn command and runtime attempt.
Retain actor, delegation and input taint for the exchange rather than inferring them from the transcript.

transcript-erasure.reason: GaugeApp agent transcript erasure writes its erasure facts directly; erasure must keep the causal record while removing content, and must not reopen access to erased payloads.
required_evidence: Erasure is an admitted command whose record keeps identifiers and causes but no erased content.
Inspection after erasure shows the erasure and refuses the content.

imported-history.reason: Legacy transcript migration and federated hand-off import command history that GaugeDesk did not mediate; it is evidence observed from elsewhere and must carry that ceiling rather than read as a fully witnessed action.
required_evidence: Mark imported records with their provenance class (legacy, imported, externally observed) and the observer that admitted them.
Never attribute an imported record to an author or request identity the source did not record.

scim-command-receipts.reason: SCIM provisioning retains its own token-authenticated membership command and standing receipt directly in the product ledger, before the shared product action admission covers hosted identity adapters.
required_evidence: Admit SCIM membership changes through the shared product action admission with exact actor, tenant, request identity, and outcome.
Keep the hosted GaugeVault standing fence and its exact denial or activation receipt in the same committed product effect.
